craft_claim: There is no reliable evidence that writing one's disclosures produces a therapeutic benefit; the intimate tone must be justified as reader-facing craft, not as catharsis or self-help.

supporting_evidence.location: GMS Psycho-Social-Medicine; meta-analysis of 30 randomized controlled trials (PMC2736499)
supporting_evidence.note: The meta-analysis found minor-to-no significant effects of expressive writing on somatic or psychological health, contradicting the earlier confident therapeutic claim.
The original study reported fewer health-centre visits after writing about trauma, but the authors labelled the findings preliminary; it is the origin of a claim later not robustly replicated.

counterevidence.note: Some physical-health benefits have been reported, and expressive writing may help some writers; the null is about reliable therapeutic benefit, not about whether writing can feel useful.
Popular vulnerability literature (Tier 4) asserts a cathartic/connective benefit, but it is not peer-reviewed evidence and is not used here to support the mechanism.

scope: Any author-side justification for using the tone; prevents 'writing it out heals' reasoning from entering card §2 or §4.
exceptions: Reflective or therapeutic private writing whose audience is the writer alone; that is tone-reflective, not tone-intimate.
